title: FALTERING LIPS AND A FAITHFUL GOD

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Now when the Lord spoke to Moses in Egypt, he said to him, "I am the Lord. Tell Pharaoh king of Egypt everything I tell you." But Moses said to the Lord, "Since I speak with faltering lips, why would Pharaoh listen to me?"" - Exodus 6:28-30 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The chapter closes almost exactly where the middle of it stood. God says, I am the Lord, tell Pharaoh everything. Moses says, but my lips falter.

He has now raised this objection several times. It is honest, and it is real, and it is also becoming a loop.

Some of us have a similar loop. The same insecurity, the same "but", brought to God again and again. There is grace in that — God keeps listening. But there comes a point where the question is no longer seeking an answer; it is avoiding an assignment.

Notice what God keeps offering as the antidote. Not a promise that Moses will become eloquent. Just the repeated declaration: I am the Lord. The remedy for a small view of ourselves is a large view of God.

Paul had a weakness he asked God three times to remove. God did not remove it, but said His grace was sufficient (2 Cor 12:8-9). Paul stopped asking and started boasting in weakness instead.

Your faltering lips are not the deciding factor. The Lord is.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What objection do I keep repeating to God instead of obeying?
2. Would a bigger view of God shrink the problem I keep circling?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, You are the Lord — that is enough. Quiet my repeated excuses and give me courage to simply obey. Amen.
